# coop-msa_v2-git-gemini-3-flash-core-low-comm-combined

<!-- Generated by tools/export_results.py. Edit only the Experiment and Observations sections. -->

## Experiment

Tests **all three communication interventions combined** (Message Delivery Timing + Message Board / Threading + Message Intent Tags) on the 10-pair `core` subset with `vertex_ai/gemini-3-flash-preview` (`low` thinking, 100 steps, compaction at 28K, per-turn step counter). Evaluates whether turn-boundary message buffering recovers the pass-rate regression seen when `threading` (1/10) or `intents` (2/10) are enabled without buffered delivery.

## Observations

- Adding turn-boundary buffering recovered pass rate back to the 4/10 baseline (`3/10` clean-merge passes on `dottxt_ai_outlines_task/1655`, `openai_tiktoken_task/0`, and `pallets_jinja_task/1559`, plus `typst_task/6554` via single-branch fallback), up from 1/10 (`threading` alone) and 2/10 (`intents` alone) at lower cost (`$3.16` vs. `$3.70`).
- All 19 opened threads were resolved (19/19 = 100% resolution rate) with zero command-parse errors across 143 messages (`ACK`: 28, `Response`: 23, `FYI`: 14, `Request`: 11, `Proposal`: 8), and per-turn thread reminders dropped 34% compared with `threading` alone (from 280 to 186).
- However, merge conflicts remained high (7/10 vs. 3/10 on `delivery-timing` alone), confirming that on `gemini-3-flash-preview` (`low` thinking), passive harness-side delivery timing (`5/10`, 3 conflicts) outperforms explicit multi-flag messaging protocols.
